definitions.explanation: Indicates any and all locations without restriction. Used to express that something exists everywhere or that one can go to any place.

examples.japanese: どこにでもある{店|みせ}だ。
examples.english: It's a store you can find anywhere.

examples.japanese: このパスがあれば、どこにでも{行|い}ける。
examples.english: With this pass, you can go anywhere.

examples.japanese: コンビニはどこにでもあるので、{買|か}い{物|もの}に{困|こま}らない。
examples.english: Convenience stores are everywhere, so you never have trouble shopping.

notes:
Composed of どこ (where) + に (location particle) + でも (even/any). Functions as an adverb meaning "at/to any place" or "everywhere." A natural combination of interrogative + でも that creates an inclusive meaning.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- どこにでもある: to be found everywhere, ubiquitous
- どこにでも{行|い}ける: can go anywhere
- どこにでも{売|う}っている: sold everywhere

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- どこにでもいる{人|ひと}: an ordinary/unremarkable person (lit. a person you'd find anywhere)
- どこにでもある{話|はなし}: a common story

SIMILAR WORDS:
- どこでも: anywhere (location of action) — similar but emphasizes where an action takes place
- {至|いた}る{所|ところ}に: everywhere — more literary expression
- {何処|どこ}にも: everywhere (with positive verb); nowhere (with negative verb)
